rules.title: Prefer phishing-resistant authentication
rules.guidance: Use passkeys or another phishing-resistant authentication method when a service offers one. Passwords are not phishing-resistant.

rules.title: Use a unique password for every account
rules.guidance: Password reuse turns one service breach into a risk to other accounts.

rules.title: Use a password manager
rules.guidance: Let a reputable password manager generate and store long, random, unique passwords. Protect the manager itself with strong authentication.

rules.title: Prefer length and unpredictability over symbol recipes
rules.guidance: When you must create a password you can remember, use a long passphrase that is not based on personal facts or predictable substitutions.

rules.title: Spaces are allowed — but they are not magic
rules.guidance: A space is a valid password character and can make passphrases easier to build, but it is not magic. Security comes from the whole password: length, unpredictability and uniqueness, not from one character.

rules.title: Do not rely on composition rules
rules.guidance: Forcing uppercase, lowercase, digits and special characters creates predictable workarounds and is not a substitute for length, blocklists and rate limiting.

rules.title: Do not rotate passwords on a calendar
rules.guidance: Change a password when there is evidence or reasonable suspicion of compromise, or when it was reused in another compromised service. Do not require arbitrary periodic changes.

rules.title: Block common and compromised passwords
rules.guidance: Services should reject common, expected and compromised passwords and explain the rejection clearly.

rules.title: Allow password managers, paste and long inputs
rules.guidance: Services should permit paste/autofill, accept broad character sets including spaces, verify the password exactly as submitted, and support at least 64 characters.

rules.title: Protect recovery paths and respond quickly to compromise
rules.guidance: Secure the primary email account and recovery methods. If a password may be compromised, change it, revoke old sessions where possible and review account recovery settings.
